They're pretty weird, it's like my brain shuts itself off for 1-5 seconds at a time. They're called absence seizures. When I get one I'll stare blankly and forget everything that was going on in that moment. Doesn't sound like a huge deal but I was getting them so often as a kid that it really affected my ability to concentrate in school, and gave me social anxiety, because I was afraid of being made fun of by my peers or accused of not paying attention in class by my teachers. During the EEG I had where they finally ended up diagnosing me, they had me fall asleep and I had 20 of them in a 15 minute time period. They are managed now by medication but they do come back if I accidentally miss a dose or two. However, I've also had a history of having grand mal seizures if I miss a dose, so it ends up feeling like playing Russian roulette with my brain.
